resources.string: Three pairs of major salivary glands, seen from the front
Paired gland map
Parotid pair
The largest pair sits in front of and below the ears. Each parotid duct crosses the cheek to open opposite an upper second molar.
Submandibular pair
These glands lie mainly beneath the lower jaw. Each submandibular duct runs forward to an opening beside the lingual frenulum.
Sublingual pair
The smallest major pair lies just beneath the lining of the floor of the mouth, one gland on either side under the tongue. Several short ducts open along each sublingual fold.
Floor of the mouth: paired glands beneath the lifted tongue
Floor of mouth cutaway
Sublingual gland bed
Each elongated gland lies under the floor-of-mouth lining beside the base of the tongue. The cutaway exposes the lobulated tissue beneath the fold.
Ducts of Rivinus
These short ducts lead from the sublingual gland to separate openings along the fold. The illustration shows only some of them.
Sublingual fold
The gland raises a ridge in the lining of the mouth. Small sublingual ducts open along the ridge rather than all draining through one opening.
Sublingual caruncle
One small bump sits on either side of the frenulum at its base. The submandibular duct opens on this bump; a larger sublingual duct may join it nearby.
Lingual frenulum
This midline fold connects the underside of the lifted tongue to the floor of the mouth and separates the paired caruncles.
Wharton duct
This longer duct carries saliva from the submandibular gland forward to the caruncle. It passes on the inner side of the sublingual gland and is distinct from the short ducts of Rivinus.
Main pancreatic duct: tail to duodenum, anterior view
Main duct cutaway
Tail tributaries
Small ducts from the lobules converge near the narrow tail to form the beginning of the main pancreatic duct.
Main pancreatic duct (Wirsung)
The main duct runs inside the pancreas. It receives smaller branches as it carries pancreatic juice from the tail through the body toward the head.
Duct bend in the head
In the broad head of the pancreas, the main duct curves toward the wall of the descending duodenum, where it usually joins the common bile duct.
Major duodenal papilla

This small projection marks the outlet in the inner wall of the descending duodenum. In the common arrangement shown here, the two ducts share a short channel, the hepatopancreatic ampulla, just before the opening.
